rhp-01.a.text: The firm adds output validation and human review to a claims model, cutting the rate of wrong denials.
rhp-01.a.why: The probability of the harm actually falls. Reduction is the only treatment that makes the affected person better off.
rhp-01.b.text: The firm buys an insurance policy covering the cost of wrongly denied claims, leaving the model unchanged.
rhp-01.b.why: The claimant is denied at exactly the same rate; only the firm's balance sheet is protected. Insurance is never a control.

rhp-02.a.text: After assessment, the emotion-inference feature is cancelled and removed from the roadmap.
rhp-02.a.why: The activity stops, so the exposure goes to zero. Avoidance is the only treatment with no residual risk to record.
rhp-02.b.text: After assessment, the emotion-inference feature ships with confidence thresholds, subgroup evaluation and human review of low-confidence cases.
rhp-02.b.why: The activity continues at lower likelihood of harm. Substantial mitigation is still reduction, and residual risk still needs an owner.

rhp-03.a.text: The deployment pipeline refuses to promote a model whose fairness evaluation has regressed past a threshold.
rhp-03.a.why: The rule executes on every release without anyone choosing to apply it, so deadline pressure cannot erode it.
rhp-03.b.text: The release checklist requires the release manager to confirm that the fairness evaluation has not regressed.
rhp-03.b.why: Identical intent, enforced by human diligence. This is the single most common over-crediting in AI risk assessments.

rhp-04.a.text: The agent's ability to issue refunds is removed from its tool set entirely.
rhp-04.a.why: No capability, no failure mode, and nothing left to monitor. Elimination is the top tier because it retires the whole branch of the risk tree.
rhp-04.b.text: The agent keeps its refund tool, with a hard limit of one refund per session and an amount cap enforced by the tool.
rhp-04.b.why: A strong technical constraint that still leaves a bounded exposure — and leaves the cap itself as something that can be misconfigured.

rhp-05.a.text: The assistant detects and blocks confidential-looking input before it is sent to the model.
rhp-05.a.why: The system prevents the disclosure regardless of what the user does. The burden sits with the party able to carry it.
rhp-05.b.text: The assistant displays a notice asking users not to paste confidential information.
rhp-05.b.why: The same risk, with the burden moved to the user. Weakest tier, and frequently the only one implemented.

rhp-06.a.text: The risk committee records the residual risk, confirms it is within appetite, names an owner and sets a review date.
rhp-06.a.why: Acceptance is an affirmative decision with authority, an owner and a review point. That record is what distinguishes it from neglect.
rhp-06.b.text: The residual risk is known to the delivery team, is not in the risk register, and no one above the team has been told.
rhp-06.b.why: Silence is not acceptance. Without the right authority deciding, there is no treatment at all — only exposure nobody has owned.

rhp-07.a.text: A free-generation summariser over clinical notes is replaced with an extractive summariser that can only quote source text.
rhp-07.a.why: The fabrication mechanism is swapped out for one incapable of fabricating, while the purpose survives. Redesign beats tuning.
rhp-07.b.text: The same free-generation summariser is kept, with temperature lowered and a grounding instruction added to the prompt.
rhp-07.b.why: The mechanism that can fabricate is intact and merely discouraged. Useful, and structurally weaker than removing the capability.

rhp-08.a.text: Retrieval enforces the requesting user's access rights, so unauthorised documents are never returned.
rhp-08.a.why: The harm cannot occur. Prevention is what reduces likelihood; everything else reduces only duration or impact.
rhp-08.b.text: A quarterly audit samples answers and reports any that cited documents the user should not have seen.
rhp-08.b.why: The disclosure already happened, up to three months ago. Detection limits impact and is routinely mistaken for prevention in control catalogues.
